notes.title: 장 보기
notes.text: Going grocery shopping is 장을 보다. Traditional markets (전통 시장) are cheaper and friendlier than supermarkets, and sellers often throw in a little extra (덤) for regulars.

notes.title: The holy trinity of jang
notes.text: Korean cooking rests on fermented sauces (장): 간장 (soy sauce), 된장 (soybean paste) and 고추장 (red pepper paste). Grandmothers often make their own and store them in big clay pots (장독).

notes.title: Tasting words
notes.text: 싱겁다 (bland), 짜다 (salty), 맵다 (spicy), 달다 (sweet), 시다 (sour), 쓰다 (bitter), 고소하다 (nutty, savory — sesame oil!), 느끼하다 (greasy, too rich).

notes.title: 김장
notes.text: Every late autumn, families gather to make a whole winter's worth of kimchi in one go (김장). Neighbors help each other and share fresh kimchi with boiled pork (수육). UNESCO lists it as Intangible Cultural Heritage.

lessons.goal: Talk about favorite foods and fusion dishes.

scene.ko: 오늘은 내가 요리할게! 퓨전 요리야. 김치 치즈 볶음밥!
scene.en: Tonight I'm cooking! Fusion food. Kimchi cheese fried rice!

scene.ko: 김치에 치즈? 진짜 맛있어?
scene.en: Kimchi with cheese? Is that really good?

scene.ko: 당연하지! 버터에 볶으면 더 맛있어. 그리고 오븐에 소시지도 구울게.
scene.en: Of course! Fried in butter it's even better. And I'll bake some sausages in the oven too.
b: to grill, to bake, to roast

scene.ko: 이건 밀가루야? 뭐 만들어?
scene.en: Is this flour? What are you making?

scene.ko: 떡볶이 소스에 식빵을 찍어 먹을 거야. 내 특별 메뉴!
scene.en: I'm going to dip bread in tteokbokki sauce. My special menu!

scene.ko: 민준아, 너는 카레도 잘하고 국수도 잘하고 초밥도 잘하잖아. 식당을 해!
scene.en: Min-jun, you're good at curry, noodles and even sushi. Open a restaurant!

scene.ko: 식당은 비싸. 그래서… 푸드 트럭을 하고 싶어.
scene.en: A restaurant's too expensive. So… I want to run a food truck.

scene.ko: 좋은 생각이야! 갈비탕, 설렁탕 같은 국 메뉴도 넣어.
scene.en: Great idea! Put soups like galbitang and seolleongtang on the menu too.
b: to be good, to be nice

notes.title: Korean fusion
notes.text: Some of Korea's favorite foods are fusion: 부대찌개 (army stew with sausage and ham), cheese tteokbokki, and kimchi fried rice topped with cheese. Food trucks (푸드 트럭) appear at night markets along the Han River.
